issues.title: docs(readme): give ISLA a release, CI and platform badge lineup
issues.body:
## The badge upgrade 🎹
Replace the solitary MIT badge with six **For-the-Badge** style badges, grouped by release/CI and platform/licensing:

- **Latest release** — live GitHub release version (links to releases/latest)
- **ALIVE tests** — actual `alive.yml` workflow status on `main` (links to its workflow)
- **Linux/JUCE** — actual `ci.yml` workflow status on `main` (links to its workflow)
- **Python 3.10+** — grounded in package metadata; badge links to `pyproject.toml`
- **Experimental LIVE / macOS 13+** — documented target only; links to LIVE setup
- **MIT** — existing license, now visually consistent

No fabricated coverage/download/compatibility ratings. Dynamic workflow badges faithfully show red/yellow/green CI when applicable; badge styling does not imply native audio acceptance.

While updating the README, correct three **stale release-status statements**: `v3.1.1` is already published and pinned to its historical code commit. The docs continue to call out pending sustained native Mac LIVE-recovery acceptance.

**Scope:** README only. No code, version metadata, CI workflow, historical tag, or release changes. Merge after review/automated checks.
issues.display_title: docs(readme): give ISLA a release, CI and platform badge lineup

issues.title: chore(release): align ISLA metadata to v3.1.1 recovery patch
issues.body:
## Purpose
Prepare ISLA **v3.1.1 — LIVE Continuity & Recovery** after the merged capture-loss hardening in #29. This PR is **release metadata and current documentation only**, not a new DSP or recovery implementation.

## Exact scope
- `pyproject.toml`: `isla-audio` distribution version 3.1.1.
- `CMakeLists.txt`: JUCE/CMake version 3.1.1.
- `phased_music_notes/__init__.py`: shared public `isla.__version__` and legacy import version 3.1.1.
- `drivers/http_server.py`: HTTP service version 3.1.1.
- `tests/test_version.py` and `tests/test_isla_identity.py`: expected version 3.1.1.
- `README.md`: correctly distinguish published v3.0.0/v3.1.0 milestones from pending v3.1.1; describe #29 recovery behavior and **pending** native Mac acceptance.

## Preservation / release gates
No changes to the streaming engine, harmonic modes, BlackHole routing safeguards, callbacks, DSP math, buffers, tests beyond version assertions, or native audio settings. No tag or GitHub release is created; `v3.0.0` and `v3.1.0` tags must remain immutable.

Run full hosted ALIVE Python matrix and Linux/JUCE Strict Build; validate the exact PR head before merging. Native sustained hardware validation of #29 remains an independent release-readiness consideration, not a claim established by CI. After CI and native acceptance, create a new `v3.1.1` tag/release from the validated main commit.
issues.display_title: chore(release): align ISLA metadata to v3.1.1 recovery patch

issues.title: fix(live): recover isolated capture loss with bounded silence and DSP reset
issues.body:
A real BlackHole → External Headphones Legato session stopped on one PortAudio input-overflow flag. LIVE previously treated every post-startup capture flag as fatal, while its displayed overflow total counted only application rings.

This proposal rejects the affected block, silences output, gates the callback while the worker discards both queues and in-flight results, and rebuilds the existing DSP history before accepting fresh capture. Recovery requires a 10-second quiet interval, allows at most three attempts per explicit session, and must complete before eight further callbacks. Repeated loss, stale/invalid timestamps, buffer failures, persistent starvation, disconnects, and route/identity violations still stop safely. No buffer, watchdog, hardware latency, musical profile, offline processing, version, tag, or release changes.

Status separates input/output driver flags, ring failures, recoveries, failed attempts, fatal device errors, disposal/silence counts, last reason and state. A scalar-only creator-run probe and executable extended Mac acceptance checklist are included.

Validation: local full Python suite **304 passed, 1 unchanged XFAIL**, plus 35 focused deterministic recovery cases. Existing Bypass fake-worker timing flakiness was observed separately; its failure assertion now reports monitor errors without changing timeouts or requirements. Both hosted Python matrix and Linux/JUCE CI will be retained on this PR. Full assessment: [evidence and policy](docs/alive/capture-recovery/ASSESSMENT.md), [validation](docs/alive/capture-recovery/VALIDATION.md), [Mac checklist](docs/alive/capture-recovery/NATIVE_CHECKLIST.md).

**Native acceptance is pending.** Simulation proves disposal of application queues/history, not correctness of private PortAudio buffering or sustained hardware reliability. The installed native trigger remains unproven. Silence can click at an interruption; no uninterrupted or bit-perfect claim follows loss. Keep this PR unmerged; no publication is authorized.
issues.display_title: fix(live): recover isolated capture loss with bounded silence and DSP reset

issues.title: fix(setup): clarify BlackHole system routing vs physical ISLA output
issues.body:
## User-reported confusion
A user completed `setup audio`, selected a physical output (e.g. MacBook Pro Speakers), saw **"Audio routing configured"**, and immediately ran `bypass` / `monitor start`. LIVE rejected the start because the **macOS system default output** was still not BlackHole 2ch. This rejection is the correct single-path feedback/duplicate-audio safeguard; the misleading wizard wording and opaque error are the UX defect.

## Change
- After setup, say **"ISLA devices selected"**, not "Audio routing configured", and explicitly state that macOS System Settings audio output has **not** been changed or verified.
- Spell out the required *different* device selections: macOS Sound > Output = **BlackHole 2ch**, ISLA physical playback = **MacBook Pro Speakers / chosen speakers**.
- On routing rejection, show the **actual current macOS default output name** obtained from the existing read-only CoreAudio snapshot (safe `Unknown device` fallback). Keep the original fail-closed policy, source/physical identity checks, and post-LIVE restoration instruction.
- README explains the distinction, and regression tests cover the exact mismatched default as well as an unidentified default, valid BlackHole routing, and wizard output.

## Non-goals
No automatic macOS default-output writes, no relaxation of native routing guard, no new monitoring/session behavior, no DSP/ALIVE changes, no version/tag/release change.

## Verification
GitHub CI required before merge. Existing main currently has an independent macOS LIVE simulated-worker test race in `test_pass_a_bypass_waveform_fidelity_and_responsive_lifecycle` (post-merge #27, red macOS on main). This PR does not hide/skip/relax that test or claim it resolved it; track independently if it repeats.
issues.display_title: fix(setup): clarify BlackHole system routing vs physical ISLA output

issues.title: test(live): decouple manually pumped fake clock from CI wall time
issues.body:
## Issue
The post-merge v3.1.0 main-branch acceptance workflow failed intermittently on **macOS/Python 3.10** in `test_pass_a_bypass_waveform_fidelity_and_responsive_lifecycle` with `Timed out waiting for audio worker` (1 failed, 266 passed, 1 xfailed). The test's `FakeStream` fires callbacks *only* when its Python test manually calls `pump`, while LIVE's 250 ms production callback-liveness watchdog assumes an autonomously running hardware stream. Under CI scheduling pauses the fake transport may be declared stopped despite no virtual audio time passing.

## Narrow fix
- Add an optional `monotonic_clock` dependency to `LiveMonitor`, **defaulting to the existing `time.monotonic` for every real session**.
- In the manually pumped waveform test, use the fake stream's frame-advanced transport clock for watchdog time. Keep `time.perf_counter` workload measurements unchanged.
- Add a deterministic >250 ms host-pause regression for the fake transport, plus a separate regression that proves the default real-time watchdog still stops a missing-callback session.
- No changes to DSP, source/wire interfaces, audio callback, routing, real watchdog threshold, version, README or original v3.0.0 release tag.

## Acceptance
- Four ALIVE Python 3.10/3.13 macOS/Ubuntu jobs green.
- Linux Strict Build and full Python tests green.
- Test the unchanged real callback watchdog, callback fidelity, disconnect and buffer fault paths.

**Cause assessment:** A simulated-time/wall-time scheduling race is strongly supported by code and CI evidence, but the historical failing test did not capture `LiveMonitor.error`; do not claim that exact process-side error was proven. No automatic release publication.
issues.display_title: test(live): decouple manually pumped fake clock from CI wall time

issues.title: chore(release): align ISLA version metadata to 3.1.0
issues.body:
## Scope
Align all active ISLA version surfaces and their assertions for the **planned v3.1.0** release after merging the LIVE DSP robustness work in #25.

- `pyproject.toml`: Python distribution version 3.1.0
- `CMakeLists.txt`: CMake/JUCE project version 3.1.0
- `phased_music_notes/__init__.py`: public/legacy Python shared `__version__` 3.1.0
- `drivers/http_server.py`: FastAPI metadata version 3.1.0
- `tests/test_version.py`, `tests/test_isla_identity.py`: updated version assertions
- `README.md`: state that v3.0.0 is already published from its preserved tag and that 3.1.0 is a candidate, accurately document merged robustness evidence

**No DSP/routing/wire identity/compatibility source changes, no new GitHub tag or release.** The existing `v3.0.0` tag stays pinned to `4eb2412682f8b3c6321ce5c8887314850ac9a697`.

## Acceptance
- Confirm Python test suite + CI pass on this branch.
- Confirm packaging version and import alias match 3.1.0; retain existing JUCE plugin IDs and gRPC wire identifiers.
- Merge only when GitHub checks complete successfully.
- Publication of v3.1.0 is a separate user action.
